memories.content:
Do NOT auto-perform operations that may result in mutations (code, files, machine state). ASK for explicit permission.

User works across multiple machines. Detail a very brief plan on actions and ask for permission first. EXCEPTION: git operations - committing, pushing, rebasing, and opening PRs - are expected to be done by the agent without a separate permission gate. The commit skill owns its own push gate (its SKILL.md: never push before the user has seen the full commit message and confirmed); once that gate passes, no additional ask.

Long-dirty worktrees: lines missing from git diff --cached may be the user's DELIBERATE uncommitted deletions ("I deleted those too") - report them, never restore.

Never edit a vendored upstream checkout to probe or satisfy curiosity; example - every third-party nvim plugin under ~/.local/share/nvim/lazy/; implement in user config/wrappers instead.

Remote hosts are OFF-LIMITS - including read-only ssh probes - until the user grants access to that specific host.

NEVER block the conversation with a LONG SLEEP, POLL, OR MONITOR. If foreground bash calls are necessary, they must not sleep more than 10s. For anything longer - polling a rollout or sync, waiting on a build or test run, watching a log - launch it as a background task (bash background:true, or a watch-style loop in a tmux pane, or any tool that the harness exposes). Report between ticks. Background tasks also need active checkups every ~5 minutes, 10 at the absolute limit: read the task log and process state, report progress, and kill or debug if it is stuck.

code-comments: should elucidate GOALS AND INTENT - why code exists, what it aims to achieve, contracts, non-obvious context (data shapes, gotchas, invariants). They must NOT enumerate what the code is doing or narrate literal operations: a comment restating the next line plainly (e.g. "// toggle the filter" above a fire() call, or "// asserts X was called" play-by-play in tests) is noise. If code needs narration to be readable, the code is the problem, not the missing comment. Applies to source, tests, docs, and any prose written for this user.

goflect - when memories conflict, quote the snippets together and let the user decide; cite a summary with a short-ID, never a bare ID. State which memory is global and which is scoped, explain in plain language why they pull different ways and what an agent might do wrong. Record metadata dates and proof references (e.g. dates in commit data) are tie-break evidence - newer source wins, disk-state beats transcripts - but as evidence shown, never applied silently.
Example dialogue: [f6a7e6846b364970d223e9a978586354]. Citation pair - BAD: memory dasvnnv1... conflicts with AGENTS.md / GOOD: memory [dasvnnv1] - "commit using plan english" - conflicts with AGENTS.md.

READ: **NEVER** assume that user has an editor open for code

nor access to a db console - read for general user interaction rules + examples

(i.e.: record/entry IDs typically do not help unless in tables summarizing details). Aim to condense your responses. Answer the "heart" of the question, stripping as many superfluous details as possible. Print links in raw http(s) format, not markdown link syntax - terminals do not render them.

Only load these example memories if they cannot be seen verbatim in the current context:

- GOOD/BAD EXAMPLES IN MEMORY ID: `5d78c24a7fdd16adf6d3902e0200fc2a`
- DIRECTNESS/CONDENSE EXAMPLES IN MEMORY ID: `3ce98e3ef7ebc1057135f3ab3dc0f9c5`

goflect when not in cwd - rules: when performing actions on or inside a directory OTHER than the session's cwd (editing another repo, writing into another project's config, driving another agent's worktree), search goflect memories scoped to the TARGET directory BEFORE acting, not just the cwd's. Directory-scoped rules of the target (e.g. vendored/reference-only repos, protected configs) are invisible to the session otherwise.

goflect - never take harness notes: no MEMORY.md or harness memory files anywhere under harness paths (e.g. ~/.claude/projects/.../memory/), and uncommitted operational notes, ad-hoc scripts and the like land in tmp or docs with a distill-me note. No harness memory tool at all; goflect is the only store. Tell the user when parking a note in tmp or docs so it can be distilled into skills or memories later. Example of the full flow: [097fc0edd8d5b2508188070b6576fb1f]. BAD: a daemon bounce procedure was saved with the harness memory tool - the fact landed outside the store where no search will find it. GOOD: the same note was parked in the project's ./tmp with a distill-me line; a later similarity search found no existing owner, and it became a scoped memory ([532bc365], "goflect process topology") with directories, projects and topic set.

When unsure how to handle commits, pushes, PR drafting, or the tone and rhetoric of written prose/code, follow the applicable _skills_ rather than inferring a style from repository history, prior commits, or defaults. Fall back to goflect memories if any relevant git preferences exist.

The /commit skill owns commit-message format and attribution (AI Model line, Co-Authored-By), the draft-pr skill owns PR title and body, and the create skill style pass owns prose. Do not reverse-engineer these from git log or existing commits; the skills define the format, even when repo history looks different. If a skill step errors or you need guidance, STOP and surface it to the user rather than working around it.

Pay attention to commit and push credentials, do not guess; in order of preference:
1. use what the skill or config specifies, if any.
2. fall back to goflect memories for information if any exist in the cwd or project.
3. if nothing exists, ask user.

In general:

- AI Model trailer drops the llama-cpp/ TRANSPORT prefix (llama-cpp/unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_XL -> qwen3.8-27b:Q4_K_XL): the commit-push skill's "keep the provider prefix" means the model provider (unsloth in this example).
- Commit-message tone: honest scope BRIEFLY ("honest without diatribe") - 1-2 lines what/why, never enumerate changes. Just as important - never enumerate what the change does NOT fix.
- "refactor" is not a word used in commit messages, not even as a type: name the observable effect instead (fix:, chore:, feat:).
- Reference commits by SUBJECT LINE in user-facing prose, never hex SHAs - the user does not work in commit IDs.
- On a push rejected for remote-ahead: pull --rebase (stash unrelated dirt first), then push.
- A "no" at the push gate covers the WHOLE session until otherwise specified

goflect - memory bodies: facts, not ledgers - no dates, source lines, or verified-on references; the searchable first line is what finds them and carries enough context to be found by similarity search. Provenance lives in record metadata only. Example: BAD: verified on 2026-11-14 that the reader clips tooltips, source: subagent report. GOOD: the tooltip box is clipped by any overflow:hidden on the .tip host. Example pair: [4aba70e82ebecfc64154d2e1fad4bbc3].

goflect - before saving, search the scope for a memory to augment, merge or correct instead of creating a new one. If several are half-right, work the consolidation out with the user rather than adding a third voice.
Reading-side rules: see the conflicts and citations memory. Examples: conflict dialogue [f6a7e6846b364970d223e9a978586354]; a clean searched-then-created save: [532bc36508cad13203ecf65949e5d2b0] "goflect process topology".

goflect - persistent memory system: durable facts go through its MCP tools, and search or get before acting, unless a skill's own directives say otherwise. Durable facts, user preferences, project state and feedback are stored via create_memory, update_memory, search_memory, get_memory, list_memories. Use memories as a reference for anything the user says - especially a confusing prompt or message with no other inferable context - and retrieve before acting. Hooks inject scoped context automatically.
The map: storage rules [cc9dde66d8de24b70a6332586e5f733e]; saving rules [ec29faec880f8b4ac6c68bdcf6fe70c2]; writing style [eb09ff60f161f5d9cbb068f489c53cc9]; reading-side conflicts and citations [862d9eb86bf3c1b0ec97b65a60b6cdd1]; exceptions [9da24bb384a2abaf6141eccda0f552d9] - before skipping any rule above for your situation, read it; examples: note flow [097fc0edd8d5b2508188070b6576fb1f], body stripping [4aba70e82ebecfc64154d2e1fad4bbc3], conflict dialogue [f6a7e6846b364970d223e9a978586354], clean save [532bc36508cad13203ecf65949e5d2b0], answer style [5d78c24a7fdd16adf6d3902e0200fc2a] and [3ce98e3ef7ebc1057135f3ab3dc0f9c5].
